turns.query: Align Kenneth French 10-industry daily returns with OFR FSI. Use 2018-2022 as training and 2023-2025 as test. Select the five industries with greatest training sample volatility, ties alphabetically, and order them by that rule. Report counts, ordered canonical Ken French industry tokens, and the maximum test OFR date/index. Carry the cohort and panels forward and interpret the risk-screen scope.

On the carried training returns in decimals, let k be the ceiling of 5% times the observation count and solve the long-only finite-sample Rockafellar-Uryasev linear program using coefficient 1/k on every nonnegative tail slack. Require weights to sum to one, cap each at 0.35, and require portfolio sample mean at least the equal-weight cohort mean. Require an optimal finite HiGHS solution and fail otherwise. Define empirical VaR as the kth-largest positive loss and CVaR as the mean of the k largest losses. Report ordered weights, optimized mean, VaR/CVaR, equal-weight CVaR, k and the infinity norm of violations across weight sum, lower/cap bounds, mean floor and all tail-slack inequalities. Carry weights forward and interpret binding-risk and estimation limits.

Hold weights fixed on 2023-2025. Report compounded return, sample volatility annualized with 252 trading days, maximum drawdown and 5% historical CVaR loss, plus equal-weight CVaR and whether optimized is lower. Interpret in-sample optimization versus held-out tail performance.

On the ten highest-OFR test dates, ties earlier, report count/mean FSI, optimized and equal-weight mean realized losses (negative return), and the optimized portfolio's largest-loss date/value. Interpret the relationship between OFR selection and portfolio losses and the ten-date sample limit.
